title: Delete the dictionary entirely
description:
Delete one of the dictionaries entirely, so it no longer exists.

Python-Gym adaptation: since a function argument's `del` only removes that local name and cannot make the caller's dictionary disappear, implement this as `delete_dictionary(student)`, which empties the dictionary of every key it holds (so nothing is left in it) and returns the now-empty dictionary as confirmation.
hints: You can't make the caller's variable itself vanish from inside a function, so the way to simulate 'the dictionary is gone' here is to strip it of everything it contains.
Dictionaries have a method whose whole purpose is to wipe out every key-value pair at once, leaving the dictionary object itself but with nothing inside.
Call the dictionary's `.clear()` method on it to wipe out every key at once, then return the dictionary (it will now be `{}`).
expected_behavior: Removes every key-value pair from the dictionary and returns it, now empty.
explanation: The clear() method removes every key-value pair from a dictionary in place, which is the closest observable equivalent - within a function boundary - to the original exercise's `del` on the whole dictionary variable.
